course.title: Control Systems
course.department: Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering

content.value: A common actuator or plant in control systems is the DC motor. It directly provides rotary motion and, coupled with wheels or drums and cables, can provide translational motion. The electric equivalent circuit of the armature and the freebody diagram of the rotor are shown in Fig. 1(b1).

The physical parameters for the motor are: J, b, Ke, Kt, R, L that have their usual meaning. The input of the system is the voltage source (v) applied to the motor’s armature, while the output is the rotational speed of the shaft 𝜃. The rotor and shaft are assumed to be rigid. We further assume a viscous friction model, that is, the friction torque is proportional to shaft angular velocity.
The motor is considered as the plant of a unity feedback control system. In this system, an inverter amplifier of 1. (b2) is used as the controller to drive the plant.
Determine the transfer function of the motor, controller, and the system. Also, find the steady state response to a standard step input.

A common example of a two-input control system is a home shower with separate valves for hot and cold water. The objective is to obtain (1) a desired temperature of the shower water and (2) a desired flow of water. Sketch a block diagram of the closed-loop control system.
